title: attention-drift-retrieval-sweep-probe
body:
Purpose and quick summary:
This doc captures an exploratory sweep focused on a class of failure modes we are calling "attention drift" (local attention weights slowly degrading fidelity to long-range retrieval context) and associated retrieval-window stress. The goal: produce reproducible prompt sets and a small regression harness targeting 8k / 32k / 128k operating points and to surface reproducible failure fingerprints (truncation cascades, silent token suppression, hallucination bursts) that we can use as guardrails during onboarding of new models.

Top-line findings (short):
- Models differ in how they degrade when retrieval contexts are appended incrementally. Two main modes observed: (A) abrupt truncation edge where earlier context is dropped cleanly but downstream generation remains stable; (B) gradual attention drift where answers slowly lose grounding and hallucination probability increases.
- KV-cache regeneration helps in mode (B) but is sensitive to alignment of cached keys across chunk boundaries — we see worst-case when retrieval inserts cross-chunk tokens at boundary alignment offsets.
- 128k runs expose emergent non-linear failure: seemingly small increases in retrieval set size produce disproportionate hallucination spikes at ~110k effective tokens for one candidate model.

Background / motivation:
- We onboard models frequently; production apps rely on a mixture of retrieval-augmented prompts (RAG) and long user context. Existing smoke tests cover truncation but not the slow-degradation cases that manifest as latent hallucination or subtle answer drift.
- This sweep is intentionally noisy: we want quick, human-readable artifacts (prompt sets + diffed model outputs) for model reviewers and SRE to reproduce.

Experimental design (high level):
- Models: two internal candidate checkpoints (C1, C2) and a public baseline (B1).
- Operating points: three context-length regimes: 8k, 32k, 128k. For each, we run progressive append tests and single-shot full-context tests.
- Retrieval patterns: contiguous chunk append, interleaved insertion (retrieved doc fragments inserted between user tokens), and prefix-heavy retrieval (large retrieved preface + short user query).
- Metrics captured: hallucination_rate (binary label by golden answers), grounding_score (exact-match / partial-match heuristics), perplexity-on-reference-blocks, token-deletion-events (where model omits referenced facts), latency and KV-cache misses.

Prompt sets (examples and variants):
- Seed story + QA chain (used to detect recall drop):
  * seed_story.txt: 8 paragraphs (~3.2k tokens) summarizing a fictional product timeline with named entities and dates.
  * QA template: "Using the story above, answer: When did Acme release version 2? Provide cite span."
  Variants: small probe (add one 100-token retrieved doc), medium (add 4 retrieved docs interleaved), large (append 15 retrieved docs totalling ~90k tokens).

- Instruction-following robustness probe (detects attention sink):
  * Task: step-by-step recipe transformation with 6 cross-references to earlier steps. We measure when the model starts producing inconsistent steps or drops references.

- Retrieval-hardness probes (synthetic near-duplicates):
  * Create many near-duplicate paragraphs with small token shifts and observe if model picks the most recent/closest span or drifts to an older duplicate.

Test matrix (simplified):
- For each model M in {C1, C2, B1}:
  for window in {8k, 32k, 128k}:
    for pattern in {contiguous, interleaved, prefix-heavy}:
      for insertion_strategy in {align-boundary, misalign-1-8-16}:
        run n=20 samples from each prompt set, record metrics and raw outputs

Notable failure modes observed (detailed examples):
1) Slow Gradual Drift (mode B):
- Behavior: answers remain correct for first ~50% of appended retrieval docs, then start to hallucinate subtle attribute changes (dates off by months, entity roles swapped) while preserving confident tone.
- Repro case: C2, 32k interleaved insertion with misalign-1 offset. QA probe shows grounding_score drop from 0.93 -> 0.58 across appends 6->12.
- Hypothesis: attention matrix sparsity combined with chunk-boundary misalignment reduces effective attention to earlier token spans; KV-cache keys for earlier chunks are deprioritized by the kernel selection heuristics.

2) Truncation Cascade (mode A):
- Behavior: when sequence exceeds model max context and truncation policy favors suffix-preservation, we observed a cascade where intermediate summary blocks vanish in subsequent generations causing multi-hop QAs to lose grounding entirely.
- Repro case: C1, 128k contiguous append, prefix-heavy prompt. After hitting truncation at ~101k, downstream answers return "I don't have information" or fabricate new entities.
- Mitigation idea: apply rolling summarization + token importance weighting so truncation removes low-importance tokens, not entire intermediate anchors.

3) Attention Sink Test (short bursts of silent tokens):
- Behavior: generator emits repeated low-information tokens or short loops when retrieval doc uses repetitive boilerplate sections. This looks like "attention sink" — model focuses on repeated patterns and fails to progress.
- Repro case: B1, 8k prefix-heavy with 3 repeated boilerplate paragraphs.
- Countermeasure: deduplicate retrieved docs and apply a repetition-penalty at retrieval time.

Data artifacts collected (what lives in repo):
- prompt-sets/ (text versions of the probes)
- raw-outputs/<model>/<window>/<pattern>/ (raw model responses)
- metrics/<date>/summary-<model>-<window>-<pattern>.csv (rows per sample, columns: grounding_score, hallucination_label, ppl_ref, kv_miss_rate, latency_ms)
- diffs/ (human-highlighted diffs for triage)

Short checklist for reproducing locally:
1) Checkout serving-runtime PR branch: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/511
2) Run harness: scripts/run_long_sweep.sh --model C2 --window 32768 --pattern interleaved --samples 20
3) Generate per-sample debug traces: set env DEBUG_TRACE=1 to persist attention heatmaps (note: heavy disk)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is attention drift a model architecture issue or an artifact of the kernel selection/quantization path? Need cross-hardware run (A100 vs H100) to rule out kernel scheduling artifacts.
- What is the user-facing threshold for hallucination that we'll enforce on onboarding? Propose a policy: grounding_score >= 0.85 for 32k workloads and >= 0.78 for 128k on our standard QA probe. Needs review by ML leads.
- Can rolling-summarization be automated in the runtime to provide deterministic truncation behavior? Prototype in serving-runtime PR 511 but needs load/latency tradeoff analysis.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally a checklist-style, messy doc. The raw outputs folder has the best signal; look at "diffs/C2_32k_interleaved_misaligned.pdf" for the most actionable human-readable examples.
- Slack thread: #applied-ml-long-context (see pinned message for quick run links).

Next immediate steps (owner assignments):
- Rajat: add A100/H100 cross-run scripts + reproduce top-3 failures by 2024-03-08.
- Elena: build small heuristic summarizer to preserve anchors and test for latency overheads.
- Samir: add deduplication + repetition penalty to retriever and run ablation.
- Maya (me): collect a compact golden set (10 canonical QA prompts) that we require new model checkpoints to pass before invite to Dedicated.

Appendix A: quick example prompt (one of the failed cases) - full text included for triage
[BEGIN PROMPT SNIPPET]
Product timeline: Acme launched v1 in 2016. v1.1 in 2017 introduced the widget. The quarter following launch saw 23% adoption. In 2018 the team moved to a microservice architecture... [~3200 tokens omitted for brevity in doc]
Retrieved fragment (injected between paragraphs 4 and 5): "In the Q2 2019 retrospective, product owner Jane Doe called the release a success and listed the following KPI improvements: feature X +12%, latency -34%"
Question: "According to the timeline above, who is the product owner in Q2 2019? Provide supporting span."
Expected: "Jane Doe (span: 'product owner Jane Doe')"
Observed (failure): "The product owner was John Smith (no supporting span)"
[END PROMPT SNIPPET]

If you triage only one artifact: open diff for C2_32k_interleaved_misaligned and inspect the attention heatmaps around append 9-12. There is a clear drop-off in attention mass to the golden span.

-- end of draft --
